exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns

question.text:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

\[ |A| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & \sqrt{3} & 5 \\ 0 & 8 & -1 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right|, \qquad |B| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 6 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ \end{array} \right|,\qquad |C| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right| \]
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • The matrix $A$ has identical columns: \[A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & {\color{blue}-1} & 2 & {\color{blue}-1} \\ 4 & {\color{blue}5} & \sqrt{3} & {\color{blue}5} \\ 0 & {\color{blue}8} & -1 & {\color{blue}8} \\ 1 & {\color{blue}0} & 1 & {\color{blue}0} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|A| = 0.$

  • The matrix $B$ has identical rows: \[B=\begin{bmatrix} 6 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}3} & {\color{blue}-1} \\ {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}3} & {\color{blue}-1} \\ \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|B| = 0.$

  • The matrix $C$ has a zero row: \[ C = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} \\ \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|C| = 0.$

Therefore, $|A|,$ $|B|,$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns

question.explanation:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

  • Since $A$ is a triangular matrix, its determinant is given by the product of the elements of the main diagonal: \[ \det(A) = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 4 \]

  • Since $B$ has two identical rows, we obtain \[ B= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & \sqrt{2} & 2 & 3 \\ {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}3} \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}3} \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(B) = 0. \]

Therefore, $2\det(A)+4\det(B) = 2 \cdot 4 + 4 \cdot 0 = 8.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns

question.explanation:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

  • Since $A$ has two identical rows, we obtain \[ A= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}7} & {\color{blue}3} & {\color{blue}2} \\ \sqrt 3 & 1 & 2 & 9 \\ {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}7} & {\color{blue}3} & {\color{blue}2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(A) = 0. \]

  • Since $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix, its determinant is: \[ \det(B) = 3\sqrt 2 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 3 = -3 \]

Therefore, $6\det(A)-2\det(B) = 6 \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot (-3) = 6.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns

question.text:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

\[ |A| = \left| \begin{array}{cccc} 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right|, \qquad |B| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & \sqrt 2 & 1\\ \sqrt 2 & 2 & \sqrt 2\\ -1 & \sqrt 2 & 1 \end{array} \right|,\qquad |C| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 0 & 5\\ -1 & 0 & 3\\ 2 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right| \]
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • Since $A$ is a triangular matrix, its determinant is given by the product of the elements of the main diagonal: \[ |A|=0 \cdot 0 \cdot 0 \cdot 0 = 0 \]

  • The matrix $B$ has proportional rows: \[ B = \begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}\sqrt 2 & \color{blue}1\\ \color{blue} \sqrt 2 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}\sqrt 2\\ -1 & \sqrt 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|B| = 0.$

  • The matrix $C$ has a zero column: \[ C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}0 & 5\\ -1 & \color{blue}0 & 3\\ 2 & \color{blue}0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|C| = 0.$

Therefore, $|A|,$ $|B|,$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns

question.explanation:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

  • Since $A$ is a triangular matrix, we have \[ \det(A) = 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 3 = 6. \]

  • Since $B$ has proportional columns, we obtain \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} \sqrt 3 & {\color{blue}{2}} & {\color{blue}{4}} \\ 0.57 & {\color{blue}{3}} & {\color{blue}{6}} \\ 1 & {\color{blue}{1}} & {\color{blue}{2}} \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(B) = 0. \]

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns

question.text:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

\[ |A| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 7 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\\ 14 & 2\sqrt 2 & 2 \end{array}\right|, \qquad |B| =\left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 1 & 4\\ -1 & 3 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right| ,\qquad |C| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & 0 & 0\\ 3 & -3 & 0\\ 0 & -3 & -1 \end{array} \right| \]
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • The matrix $A$ has proportional rows: \[ A = \begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}7} & {\color{blue}\sqrt 2} & {\color{blue}1} \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ {\color{blue}14} & {\color{blue}2\sqrt 2} & {\color{blue}2} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|A| = 0.$

  • The matrix $B$ has a zero row: \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 4\\ -1 & 3 & 2\\ {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|B| = 0.$

  • The matrix $C$ is a triangular matrix, hence \[ |C| = 2 \cdot (-3) \cdot (-1) = 6 \neq 0. \]

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|B|$ are equal to $0.$

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Reasons Why a Determinant Equals Zero

question.text:
Let $A$ be a $3\times 3$ matrix such that $|A|=0.$ Which of the following statements must be true?

  1. $A$ has a zero column
  2. $A$ has two proportional rows
  3. One of the rows/columns of $A$ is a linear combination of other rows/columns of $A$
question.explanation:
Let's consider our statements in turn.

  • Statements I and II are false. For example, consider the matrix \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}. \] Expending across the $1$st column, we have that \begin{align*} |A| &= 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= (3-2)+(1-2) \\[5pt] &= 0 \end{align*} but $A$ has neither a zero column nor two proportional rows.

  • Statement III is true. Indeed, we can make use of the following fact:

    $|A|=0$ if and only if one of the rows/columns of $A$ is a linear combination of other rows/columns of $A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

example.title: Identifying the Reasons Why a Determinant Equals Zero

question.text:
\[ A=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 10 & 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \]

Consider the matrix given above. Identify all of the reasons why one can conclude that $|A|=0?$

  1. $A$ has proportional rows
  2. $A$ has proportional columns
  3. $A$ has identical rows
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

  • $A$ has proportional rows: \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}5} & {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}-1} \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ {\color{blue}10} & {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}-2} \end{bmatrix} \quad{\color{green}{\checkmark}} \]

  • $A$ does not have proportional columns.

  • $A$ does not have identical rows.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

example.title: Identifying the Reasons Why a Determinant Equals Zero

question.text:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix such that $|A|=0.$ Which of the following statements must be true?

  1. One of the rows/columns of $A$ is proportional to another row/column of $A$
  2. $A$ has two identical rows
  3. $A$ has a zero row
question.explanation:
Let's consider our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, we can make use of the following fact:

    $|A|=0$ if and only if one of the rows/columns of $A$ is a linear combination of other rows/columns of $A.$

    In the case of a $2 \times 2$ matrix, this means that one of the rows/columns must be proportional to another row/column.

  • Statements II and III are false. For example, consider the matrix \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 6 & 3 \end{bmatrix}. \] We have that \[ |A| = 4 \cdot 3 - 6 \cdot 2 = 0 \] but $A$ has neither two identical rows nor a zero row.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
